header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:egy:tla:sawlit:pchester-beatty-i:translit, from the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (2018), in Simon Schweitzer's AED-TEI (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. notes.1.31: Setjet (Sṯt), restored, is probably the island of Sehel.
notes.1.66: 1.66: 'whose breath is bad' is literally 'bad of the taste of his mouth'. 1.67: 'the Thirty' (30yt) is the divine tribunal.
notes.1.121: kꜣsꜣ, taken as 'bent, stooping', is uncertain; the editor deletes a repeated kꜣsꜣ.
notes.3.5: 3.5: ḥbsj is uncertain, perhaps for ḥb-sd, 'jubilee festivals'. 3.6: the relation of 'the heir' and 'who brought you into being' to the rest is unclear. 3.8: the scribe wrote Mn-tj, which the editor reads as Min; it may stand for Montu. kꜣ may be 'ka' or 'bull'.

nodes.text: And Onuris let out a great cry before the Ennead, saying:
Then Banebdjedet, the great god who dwells in [Setjet], was brought before Atum, together with Ptah-Tatenen.
and this office is too great for you, you boy whose breath is bad.
Then Onuris raged a million times over, and so did the whole Ennead, the Thirty.
And the god Baba stood up,
and he said to Ra-Horakhty:
Your shrine is empty!
Then Ra-Horakhty was hurt by the answer that had been said to him,
and he lay down on his back, his heart very sore indeed.
Then the great god laughed at her.
Then he got up
and sat down with the Great Ennead,
and he said to Horus and Seth:
Speak for yourselves!
Now I kill the enemy of Ra every day, being at the prow of the Bark of Millions, and no other god is able to do it.
Then Onuris and Thoth let out a great cry, saying:
Cross over to the Island in the Middle and judge them there, and say to Nemty the ferryman:
She reached Nemty the ferryman as he sat close by his boat; she had changed her form into an old woman, who walked bent over(?), with a small gold signet-ring on her hand.
Thoth writes for you jubilees(?) beside the Lord of All, the king of the gods.
The heir of the greatest of the gods, Amun Kamutef, who brought you into being: he gives you all [lands] in the embrace of his strong arm, while you sit on the throne of Ra.
Great-of-Magic is upon your head.
Ramesses-Amenherkhepeshef-Meryamun, [may he live, prosper] and be healthy, the ruler who destroys the Nine Bows: [your] father Min gives you his ka.
Baal gives you strength, O divine king, beloved one, who seized the Two Lands [by] his strength.
